second_order: Making, testing, and missing the question-mark deny joke
theme_note: Participants traced Valve's question-mark deny to a Reddit suggestion, tested its date trigger, used it as a reply joke, asked to keep it, and later missed it. What varies is whether they celebrated, found it tilting, tested it, or sought a workaround after removal.

second_order: Making and sorting other April Fools jokes
theme_note: Participants made, tested, explained, challenged, or dismissed April Fools claims other than the deny symbol, r/tz makeover, and image-search effort. The variation runs from fake roster and update news to the League/Merrill front-page parody and arguments over whether these jokes displaced ordinary Dota talk.

second_order: Choosing, drawing, and enlarging Dota canvas art
theme_note: Participants chose coordinates, supplied designs, placed pixels, compared sizes, recruited help, and reported progress on Dota canvas art. What varies is the proposed spot, scale, colour, design, and whether speakers wanted a modest mark or continued enlargement.

second_order: Negotiating borders and helping canvas neighbors
theme_note: Participants asked neighbours for room, set borders, offered or refused help, and tried to avoid overwriting flags and other communities' pictures. What varies is mutual aid, permission-seeking, diplomacy through Discord, firm refusal to shrink, and opportunistic responses to requests.

second_order: Turning the subreddit into r/tz and playing along
theme_note: Participants inhabited the temporary r/tz makeover by posting Arteezy material, enforcing or bending its posting rule, explaining it, praising it, and objecting to its flood. What varies is willing play, moderation, mock devotion, confusion, and resistance.

second_order: Adding names, mangoes, and other Dota pictures
theme_note: Participants proposed and worked on additions around the main art: Dota lettering, mangoes, Kappa, HoHoHaHa, EE, Alliance, and other game-linked pictures. What varies is whether an addition gained coordinates and labour, met objections, or remained a title-only call.

second_order: Running and disputing scripts for shared art
theme_note: Participants shared, adapted, ran, corrected, and disputed scripts used to place or maintain pixels. What varies is using scripts for repair or enlargement, technical troubleshooting, conflict between versions, and objections that automation erased the fun or neighbours' work.

second_order: Repairing and defending Dota canvas art
theme_note: Participants watched the Dota logo, sounded alarms, corrected pixels, repaired damage, and handed helpers to existing defence threads. What varies is immediate repair, false alarms resolved by refresh, overnight holding, and uncertainty over who was changing pixels.

second_order: Attacking and mocking rival canvas art
theme_note: Participants called for, joined, mocked, or refused attempts to overwrite rival game art. What varies is League, Heroes of the Storm, or CS:GO as target and whether replies embraced attack, preferred improving Dota's art, or rejected retaliation.

second_order: Trying to keep or recover swapped flairs
theme_note: Participants tried to keep or recover team flairs changed during r/tz and compared what others retained. What varies is petitioning during the joke, peer explanation, moderator-directed troubleshooting, and later reports that a flair could not be restored.

second_order: Drawing and guarding Artour on the canvas
theme_note: Participants proposed, located, drew, altered, and guarded the Artour portrait. What varies is initial face-building, adding RTZ text, protecting the chin, permitting or resisting SKADOOSH, and later claims about what survived.

second_order: Playing the Fake MOBA image-search fight
theme_note: Participants tried to associate League or Dota images with phrases such as Fake MOBA, Real MOBA, Ripoff, and Pay to Win, then reported or disputed results. What varies is the search phrase, target, claimed success, copying accusation, and cross-subreddit participation.

second_order: Looking back on what the canvas made
theme_note: After placement, participants thanked makers, circulated timelapses and altered logos, claimed objectives and labour, and argued about the finished result. What varies is pride, criticism of scripts and enlargement, memories of help and conflict, and appreciation of Dota's place among other pictures.

second_order: Watching the DAC final outside the case
theme_note: These codes describe spectators watching the DAC final, not r/place or the room's April Fools conduct. They are kept together only because a fleet coder emitted them under an irreversible coded disposition; they are excluded from the case interpretation.

second_order: Carrying pixel-art making to another canvas
theme_note: Participants invited people who enjoyed r/place to build on pixls.space or pxls.space. The practice is a proposed continuation beyond Reddit; the record does not show uptake or completed work there.
